How to play

You get a start player and a target player. Name a teammate of the start player, then a teammate of that player, and keep going until you reach someone who played with the target.

  • Teammates means they were on the same team's roster in the same season.
  • You have 6 guesses. A wrong guess uses one up and does not move your current player.
  • You cannot use the same successful player twice. A teammate of the target completes the chain; guessing the target directly works too.
  • Hints can be reused, but every use is counted on your share card.
  • The puzzle's standard links use players with 10+ games for that team-season. Shorter stints still count as guesses and are marked on the link.

Daily is the same puzzle for everyone and changes at midnight Pacific time. It gets harder through the week, from warm-ups early on to extra innings on Sunday. Past puzzles are in the Puzzle menu and do not count toward streaks. Unlimited lets you pick a difficulty and keep a run going.

Optional email/password accounts let you sync daily progress and stats across devices. You can choose whether your display name and scores appear on the public leaderboard. Guests can play without signing in; guest and account saves are kept separately on shared devices.

      Baseball data: SABR Lahman Database, created by Sean Lahman and maintained by the Society for American Baseball Research (CC BY-SA 3.0). This MLB-only roster includes data through the 2025 season. Standard links use 10+ games for a team-season; shorter stints count and are labeled. All 1,100 original daily puzzles are kept (some were moved later to make room for modern-era puzzles); later dates are generated deterministically. Unlimited and generated daily puzzles deliberately include players active since 2020; “recent debut” here means a first MLB appearance in 2020 or later, not an official MLB rookie designation.
